Scenario credit losses on real data: EQB Inc.

creditloss · jump-off 2026Q2 (EQB book at July 31, 2026) · horizon 13 quarters · public data only

This is an outside-in exercise from public disclosures and public macro data, not EQB's own model. Where EQB does not disclose something (LTV distribution, card limits, amortization), the assumption is stated. Scenarios are author-built; Moody's paths are not public.

1. Results

Over 13 quarters, modelled credit losses on EQB's $49.2bn on-balance-sheet book are C$602m in the baseline (1.17% of exposure) and C$1,456m in the severe scenario (2.83%). Severe-scenario IFRS 9 provisions (write-offs plus the change in the allowance, opening from the probability-weighted allowance) are C$1,028m; section 7 has the stage-by-stage view. The newly acquired PC Financial card book is 9% of loans but carries 80% of baseline losses; uninsured mortgages, at a 69% average LTV, move most in relative terms, from C$28m to C$278m, as a 30% house-price fall pushes higher-LTV loans into collateral shortfall.

COVID bridge. Unemployment hit 13% in 2020Q2 while arrears and charge-offs fell, because of deferrals and income support. Left in, that episode drags the unemployment elasticity toward zero, so the macro series are interpolated through 2020Q2–2021Q3, the usual treatment in bank IFRS 9 models.

Data gaps. StatCan Ontario unemployment (table 14-10-0287), the BoC 5-year mortgage rate and CREA/Teranet Ontario house prices would replace the national proxies. OSB Ontario consumer and business insolvencies would replace the US charge-off proxies. This workspace was blocked from those sites.

The severe path matches the size of the Bank of England 2025 test (house prices −28%) and Ontario's early-1990s downturn (unemployment near 11%). Card and commercial satellites, which were estimated on US data, are driven by the Canadian unemployment change: the US jump-off rate plus the Canadian scenario's deviation.

PD_bank,t = PD_bank,0 × proxy_t / proxy_0 (proxy_t from the champion satellite under the scenario)
  • Mortgages and commercial. PD0 comes from EQB's impaired data. Q3 impaired formations were about $205m a quarter (Q2 formations less the disclosed $39m decline), or roughly $0.8bn a year, on $35.7bn of uninsured residential and commercial loans. Split by the Apr 30 impaired mix (personal 1.9% of uninsured personal loans, commercial 5.3%), that gives 1.7% for uninsured mortgages and 3.4% for commercial. Insured: 1.3%, from insured impaired loans of $147m.
  • Credit cards. EQB gives no card default data one month after the acquisition. PD0 is solved so the model's probability-weighted Stage 1+2 allowance equals the $239.8m EQB reports, giving 2.60% a year.
  • LTV. The disclosed 69% average is spread over four buckets (45/60/71/78%, assumed weights 10/20/35/35%). Decumulation loans are set at 35%.
  • Stage 2. Calibrated to EQB's Apr 30 shares (personal 20.4%, commercial 11.7%); cards 12% assumed.

Check: model allowance at jump-off vs EQB's reported allowance, C$m

Model, baseline only Model, probability-weighted EQB reported (Stage 1+2) Model / reported
Commercial + equipment 31.66 52.38 95.60 0.55
Credit cards 208.96 239.84 239.84 1.00
Insured mortgages 1.16 1.52 1.24 1.23
Uninsured mortgages 12.06 37.58 63.18 0.59

Only the card line was calibrated. For the three other books together, the modelled probability-weighted allowance is -43% against what EQB reports. The model discounts expected shortfalls at the loan rate and measures lifetime ECL only to the end of the contractual term (renewal for mortgages, assumed 2.5–3 years), as IFRS 9 requires, and it carries no management overlay. A longer behavioural life, a lower cure rate or an overlay would each close the gap; EQB's own inputs on these points are not public, so the gap is left visible rather than calibrated away.

Stage 3 is a separate check. EQB's total allowance at July 31, 2026 was $485.4m, which implies about $86m on impaired loans; the model's Stage 3 allowance is $68m, and its total $399m. EQB also notes impaired loans rose because of "extended workout timelines", which is why the workout period is set to six quarters for mortgages and commercial loans.

4. PD satellites

Same engine as the methodology build. The candidates are each series × transform × lag 0–4. A sign-constrained search over 1–3 drivers with an AR(1) term is run alongside literature specifications and BMA. The champion must carry the literature signs and capture 80–200% of crisis defaults out of sample. Among those, the lowest out-of-sample error wins.

Three literature equations come out with the wrong sign on unemployment on real data. They are the ECB/EBA-style mortgage equation and the unemployment-level card and commercial equations: with a near-unit-root lag, the level of unemployment adds nothing and its sign flips. They are kept in the model-risk range but cannot be champion. The mortgage champion is the TDSA-style equation (change in unemployment and house-price growth). Card and commercial champions both reduce to the change in unemployment.

Mortgages: the champion captured 124% of the 2008–10 arrears rise and 65% of the 2023–26 rise. It underpredicts the recent episode, which was driven by payment shock at renewal, a channel unemployment and house prices only partly carry. Cards: 88% and 84%. Commercial: no model meets the 80–200% band. The change-in-unemployment model over-shoots the GFC 3.4× from a 2007 origin, while the alternatives under-shoot badly. The over-shooter is kept as champion, and the commercial severe loss should be read as conservative.

7. IFRS 9 view

The stage engine tracks gross loans in Stages 1–3 every quarter. Loans move to Stage 2 when their PD passes 3× the origination PD (calibrated to EQB's reported Stage 2 shares), default into Stage 3, and leave Stage 3 after a workout period, either cured or written off. Stage 1 carries 12-month ECL, Stages 2 and 3 lifetime ECL, discounted at the loan rate. Scenario PDs are used for 12 quarters, then revert to the long-run average over 8. Every scenario opens from the probability-weighted allowance, so the first quarter's provision includes the move to that scenario's own forward-looking ECL.

In the severe scenario the allowance builds immediately (the day-one line), loans migrate into Stage 2 and Stage 3, and write-offs then draw it down as defaults are resolved. In the baseline, the allowance is released: the opening allowance carries the 30% downside and 20% severe weights, which fall away as the baseline unfolds.

8. Limitations

  • Mortgage dynamics come from big-bank Ontario arrears. EQB's alternative-lending borrowers may be more sensitive than the scaling assumes, since the scale is fixed at jump-off.
  • Card and commercial sensitivities are US-estimated. Canadian card losses rose less than US losses in 2008–10, so the card stress is likely conservative; commercial depends on construction and CRE exposure that US C&I charge-offs only roughly represent.
  • The structural mortgage LGD uses a national house-price index. GTA condo prices have fallen more than the national index since 2022, which matters for EQB.
  • Static balance sheet; no management actions; second-round effects excluded.
  • PC Financial was acquired on July 1, 2026, so the card book's own loss history is not yet in EQB's disclosures.
